body:
## Summary

`IntervalSpec` next-run calculation uses **fixed UTC second alignment** (`((ts-phase)/interval+1)*interval+phase`) and **ignores** `ScheduleSpec.timezone` for day-sized intervals. Schedules that mean “every N **local** days at a fixed local time” therefore **do not track DST** (e.g. US/Pacific: local midnight stays 07:00 UTC in PDT but should move to 08:00 UTC in PST after the fall transition).

`StructuredCalendar` / cron paths already use the loaded `*time.Location`; interval-only schedules do not.

## Reproduction (behavior before fix)

- `ScheduleSpec.timezone` = `America/Los_Angeles` (or any IANA zone with DST).
- `Interval` = `24h`, `Phase` = `8h` (first tick aligned to `1970-01-01 00:00:00` in that zone, i.e. `time.Unix(8*3600,0)` local representation).
- Observe `rawNextTime` / `GetNextTime` just after 2018-11-04 local midnight and 2018-11-05 local midnight:
  - **Before fix:** every tick is `k * 86400` seconds from the same UTC phase (e.g. always `07:00Z` in this setup).
  - **After fix:** 2018-11-04 `00:00` local is still PDT → `07:00Z`; 2018-11-05 `00:00` local is PST → `08:00Z`.

## Proposed semantics

When `interval` is a positive multiple of `86400` **and** the schedule has a **non-UTC** location, interpret the step as **N whole calendar days** in that location at the same **local** time-of-day as the grid reference `time.Unix(phase mod interval, 0).In(loc)`.

When the location is `UTC` (or unset/empty in a way that resolves to UTC), keep the **existing** fixed-UTC-second behavior for compatibility.

## Non-goals

- `43h` or other non–whole-day intervals: unchanged.
- This does not try to turn “24h” into “civil 24h” in zone for non-86400-multiple durations.

## Motivation

Common use case: `IntervalSpec` for “every N days or weeks” with an end-user or workspace-scoped IANA time zone, where local wall time should remain stable when DST changes.

comments.body: We should not complicate the very simple and predictable semantics of intervals for a calendar-related use case. If neither interval nor calendar specs address this use case (and they don't), then maybe a new spec type is appropriate. e.g. supporting RRULE would address a lot of these less common cases.

Thanks @dnr, that makes sense. We were hitting real behaviour where a **24h (86400s) `Interval` + IANA `timezone` still advanced on fixed UTC steps**, so local wall time drifted over DST, while the **calendar/cron** path *did* respect the zone. Our PR was one way to make "N×86400s" line up with **civil** days in the named zone, but I agree that **overload’s** `IntervalSpec` and blurs the line between a pure duration model and a calendar one.

We’re not tied to that particular implementation. If the intended direction is to **keep intervals minimal** and to handle this class of use cases with **something calendric** (e.g. **RRULE** or another explicit spec), we’re happy to follow that. On our side we can also map "every *N* local days/weeks" in the product to **calendar/cron/RRULE**-style data instead of reusing `Interval` if that’s the long-term story.

If you (or the team) already have a preferred direction between "RRULE in schedule" vs "express via `StructuredCalendar` + timezone only," a pointer to existing discussion or a rough timeline would help us plan downstream work. Either way, thanks for the clear constraint—it helps a lot.

**Note:** we can **rework or close** the open PR once there’s an agreed design from the maintenance team.

The problem (that you're aware of) is that "every n days from the epoch" isn't expressible with cron-style rules, and the current calendar specs are pretty much tied to cron semantics. e.g. using "*/5" in the day of month field means every 5 days from the start of the month, and gets reset with each new month). I don't have much experience with RRULE but I believe it does support that case, and a bunch of others that are impossible or awkward with cron-style rules.

I don't know exactly what the team's plans are in this area, I just want to express that time is hard enough as it is, we should try to keep semantics and mental models as simple as possible and not introduce exceptions.

Thanks, that's helpful.

We're exactly in the "every n **days** from a **civil** anchor in a `TZID`, not 'every 86400 seconds from the epoch'" case: public `IntervalSpec` is the latter (`epoch + n * interval + phase` in the API comments), and cron/calendar in Temporal don't express "every n days *from an arbitrary anchor* in the way many products mean it" the same way *day_of_month* stepping works (monthly reset, etc.).

**RRULE** (RFC 5545) is a good fit for that: `DTSTART;TZID=…` with `FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=n` or `WEEKLY` + `BY…` in a named zone is the standard way to get **calendar** recurrence and DST rules from the zone data. We're aligned with not **overloading** that onto `IntervalSpec` if the product direction is a **separate** path (e.g. RRULE or a dedicated spec) so interval stays simple and predictable.

Our open PR was one way to get local-day stepping without a new spec type; we're happy to **rework or close** it if the team prefers a cleaner split (e.g. RRULE or a new field on `ScheduleSpec`).

We don't have a strong ask on **full** RRULE on day one—a **bounded** subset (daily/weekly, `INTERVAL`, `start_time` + `timezone_name` as the DTSTART story) would already cover a lot of downstream cases.

Thanks again for spelling out the interval vs calendar semantics—it clarifies the gap.

Quick update from our side, aligned with @dnr’s feedback: we are **closing** the current PR (the one that adjusted day-sized `Interval` math for non-UTC IANA time zones) so we do not overload the documented `IntervalSpec` / epoch+phase model.

**Next step:** we plan to **open a new change** in the same area that follows a **separate, calendar-oriented** spec—**RRULE (RFC 5545)** in the spirit of the thread—with a **practical subset** to start (e.g. `FREQ`/`INTERVAL` with `DTSTART` + `timezone` / `TZID` semantics) rather than entangling that behavior into `IntervalSpec`.

We’ll use this issue for design discussion with the team before a new PR. Thanks again for the clarity on cron vs. interval vs. a dedicated recurrence form.

Thanks for the clear direction on this thread.

We’re **not** pursuing the “civil day on top of `IntervalSpec`” approach further (that PR is closed in favor of what you described here).

**What we’re doing instead:** add **calendar-style recurrence** via **`ScheduleSpec.rrule`** (RFC 5545 line bodies) and implement evaluation in the scheduler with a small RRULE library, keeping **`IntervalSpec` as simple epoch + phase** semantics. That lines up with the point that “every *n* days from epoch” in local civil time is a different product than pure interval math, and that RRULE (or a bounded subset) is a better fit for “every *n* **calendar** days/weeks in a named zone” when you care about DST and local midnights.

**Open PRs (for anyone following along):**
- **API:** https://github.com/temporalio/api/pull/773 — `repeated string rrule` on `ScheduleSpec`
- **Server:** https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/pull/10067 — union next times from existing calendar/cron/interval + RRULE

We’ll adjust the server PR to use a published `go.temporal.io/api` version once the API change lands, and we’re tracking **TypeScript / SDK** follow-up so clients can set `rrule` on the wire the same way other spec fields are set.

Appreciate the time you took on the design notes here—this path is much easier to reason about than overloading `IntervalSpec`.

title: Schedule: IntervalSpec should advance by calendar days in ScheduleSpec timezone (DST)
